name: fracture radiology overview
title: Describing a fracture on x-ray in a fixed order: views, location, type, descriptors, joint surface, other findings and bone quality, then how healing looks on follow-up films; each column gives what to look for and what it tells you

root.title: A fracture on x-ray: TRACE the cortex, look for SECONDARY signs, then describe it in the same order every time
lines: body in anatomic position · more than one descriptor for each fracture
OLD ACIDS: open · location · degree · articular surface · comminution · intrinsic bone quality · displacement · soft tissue

groups.title: DESCRIBE IT
lines: what you say on the phone so the consultant can picture it

head: h
1 · Views
anteroposterior (AP) · lateral · oblique
inv: • spiral: seen only on multiple views

head: h
2 · Location
side · which bone · where in it
inv: growth plate involved → Salter-Harris (see the PEDIATRIC ORTHOPEDICS chart)

head: h
3 · Type
complete or incomplete
inv: • avulsion: tendon pulls off a fragment

head: h
4 · Descriptors
DISTAL fragment relative to proximal
except the CLAVICLE: proximal to distal
pres: in shaft widths · more than one width = OFF-ENDED
by the apex: varus = apex LATERAL, valgus = apex MEDIAL
internal or external · look at the joints above and below

head: h
5 · Joint surface
into the joint or not?
inv: reduction relatively anatomic: bone remodels, especially with weight-bearing

head: h
8 · Healing
mostly SECONDARY (callus) · PRIMARY with internal fixation: no callus
pres: • union: bridging callus, medullary space back
inv: no tenderness, no motion at the site, can bear weight
• lower limb 6-12 weeks (femoral neck, shaft longest)

panels.title: When it does not heal
items: delayed union: takes TWICE as long as expected · non-union: no healing in 6-9 months · malunion: heals out of anatomic position
what to do about them: see the FRACTURE MANAGEMENT chart
